Back to school Family Fun Fest draws hundreds to Robert Crown

by Heidi Randhava August 23rd, 2026August 24th, 2026

People of all ages turned out for the fourth annual Evanston Family Fun Fest on Saturday at the Robert Crown Community Center organized by youth outreach nonprofit Be Strong Families in partnership with the city’s Parks and Recreation Department and Evanston Cradle to Career.

Themed “Sweet Summer Send-Off,” the free event marking the start to a new school year featured dozens of indoor and outdoor activities and honored the legacy of Dr. Marjorie Fujara, a local pediatrician remembered as a champion of trauma-informed care.

The celebration offered families a chance to say goodbye to summer feeling supported and inspired. It featured lunch fresh off the grill, inflatable carnival games, ultimate frisbee, unicyclist and juggler Kyle Campbell (a.k.a. UniKyle, shown in the video above) and soccer. Indoor fun also included ice skating, a dance-off, family portraits, arts and crafts, book giveaways, a resource fair, a puppet show and a Chicago Ballet Arts presentation.

A tribute to Dr. Fujara was held in the Robert Crown Library Room. The inaugural Family Fun Fest in 2023 was held in honor of Fujara, who was part of the first group of clinicians to be certified in a subspeciality on child abuse pediatrics.

At the event, Mayor Daniel Biss read a proclamation declaring Saturday “Evanston is Family Strong! Day” and stating that Fujara was a supporter of strong families in Evanston and Cook County “through her work as a physician and community member focusing on issues including gun violence, child physical and sexual abuse, mental health, and education policy.”

On the staff at Cook County Health and the Children’s Advocacy Center, Fujara worked to promote safety for children until her untimely death in 2021.
